title: Inflation just hit a 3-year high

lines: Inflation just hit its highest level in three years.
The Fed's favorite gauge, the PCE index,
rose 3.8% over the past year in October.
And it keeps climbing, month after month:
Wall Street now expects the Fed to RAISE rates
Card, car-loan and mortgage rates stay high.
A balance that isn't getting cheaper costs you every month.
Is a stubborn rate changing how you spend this holiday?

source_line: Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, October 2026 PCE report (Nov. 25, 2026)
caption:
Inflation just hit a 3-year high — and the rate relief everyone was counting on is on hold.

The Fed's preferred gauge, the PCE price index, rose 3.8% over the past year in October, up from 3.6% in September and the hottest reading in three years. Core PCE climbed to 3.3%; prices rose 0.3% in the month alone.

With inflation that far above the Fed's 2% goal, markets have flipped from expecting a cut to pricing in a rate INCREASE at the Dec. 9 meeting. The benchmark already sits at 3.75%–4.00%.

Why it's your money: credit-card APRs, car loans and mortgage rates all move with the Fed, so cheaper borrowing isn't coming — and could reverse. The one bright spot: high-yield savings keeps paying well.

My take: higher-for-longer stopped being a warning and became the bill. A balance that isn't getting cheaper costs you every month.

Is a stubborn card or loan rate changing how you spend this holiday season? 👇

Source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis, October 2026 PCE report (released Nov. 25, 2026)
